A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transcriptomic drug screening of neural cells from individuals with SZ and control subjects revealed that drugs that reversed SZ-associated postmortem transcriptomic signatures also differentially regulated neuropsychiatric disease associated genes in a cell-type (NPCs vs. cancer cell lines) and/or diagnosis (SZ vs control)-dependent manner.

this is the first time that we have been able to identify drugs that reverse post mortem SZ-associated transcriptomics signatures, and several of those also differentially regulate disease associated genes in a cell-type and a diagnosis-dependent manner.
our study provides a proof of concept for the utility of patient-specific cell types for the discovery of novel therapeutic strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patient-specific cell types can be used to identify drugs that target the molecular basis of disease.
patient-specific, cell type-specific, and disease-relevant drug screening platforms can be used to identify novel drug candidates and targets for psychiatric disorders.
the use of cell type and patient specific platforms in drug discovery can reveal major advantages over commonly used cancer cells.
